Step, impulse and initial-condition responses

Source: R/simulation.R
ctrl_step.Rd

  • ctrl_step(): response to a unit step (times amplitude) applied at time 0 to each selected input in turn, from zero initial state.

  • ctrl_impulse(): impulse response. In continuous time this is the response to a Dirac impulse, computed as the free response from \(x(0^+) = B e_j\). The Dirac component \(D\delta(t)\) of the output cannot be represented on a time grid and is omitted (a warning is given when D is nonzero). In discrete time the input is the unit pulse (Kronecker delta) \(u_0 = 1\), \(u_k = 0\) for \(k > 0\); no 1/dt scaling is applied, so a continuous impulse is not reproduced by a discrete pulse.

  • ctrl_initial(): free response from the initial state x0.

Usage

ctrl_step(sys, times = NULL, inputs = NULL, amplitude = 1)

ctrl_impulse(sys, times = NULL, inputs = NULL)

ctrl_initial(sys, x0, times = NULL)

Arguments

sys

A model.

times

Optional time grid (sample instants for discrete models). The step, impulse or initial state is applied at time zero; a grid that starts later reports the same response at its own instants.

inputs

Input channels (indices or names); default all.

amplitude

Step amplitude.

x0

Initial state for ctrl_initial().

Value

A ctrl_response with one case per input channel.

Details

Default time grids are chosen from the pole locations.

Examples

G <- ctrl_tf(4, c(1, 1.2, 4))
st <- ctrl_step(G)
ctrl_step_info(st)
#>   output    case rise_time settling_time overshoot undershoot     peak
#> 1     y1 step u1  0.661306      6.661667  37.10144          0 1.372324
#>   peak_time final_value settled final_value_known
#> 1     1.645    1.000955    TRUE             FALSE
plot(st)

ctrl_impulse(G, times = seq(0, 10, by = 0.05))
#> Time response (impulse, continuous time)
#>   201 time points from 0 to 10
#>   outputs: y1
